sections.title: Target Configuration & Environment Selection
sections.content:
VenvHub Pro includes an integrated visual builder to compile Python scripts (.py) into standalone Windows executables (.exe) leveraging PyInstaller.

Setup Pipeline:

  1. Project Selection: Choose the target workspace project.
  2. Source Environment: PyInstaller inspects and bundles exact package versions active in this specific virtual environment.
  3. Target Entry Script: Scans project root for runnable Python entry points (e.g. main.py).
  4. Output Destination: Where final .exe and intermediary build artifacts land (defaults to dist/ inside the project).
Automated Dependency Check: If pyinstaller is missing inside the active Venv, VenvHub detects it upon clicking 'BUILD' and provisions it in the background.

sections.title: Core Settings (Console, OneFile vs Onedir)
sections.content:
Window & Console Execution

  • Console Output: Ideal for CLI tools and debugging (displays stdout/stderr logs on crash).
  • Windowed Mode (--noconsole): Intended for production GUI applications, suppressing the background CMD console.

Packaging Topology (Performance vs Distribution)

  • Single File (--onefile): Bundles the interpreter, packages, and assets into a single distributable binary. Simple to share, but incurs a startup delay while extracting to the system Temp directory.
  • Directory Mode (--onedir): Produces an application directory with unpacked binaries. Provides instant startup performance, but requires distributing the entire directory folder.

sections.title: Bundling Data Assets & sys._MEIPASS
sections.content:
PyInstaller bundles only Python source code by default. Non-Python dependencies (images, audio, fonts, config.json) must be mapped in the Assets matrix to prevent runtime FileNotFoundError exceptions.

Asset Destination Mapping:

Source PathDestination FolderDescription
C:\Project\logo.png. (dot)Extracted directly alongside the .exe binary root.
C:\Project\ui_files\gui/templatesPreserves folder tree as gui/templates/ inside the bundle.
Critical Runtime Path Notice: In OneFile bundles, static relative paths break because files unpack into temporary directories. Use this resolution helper:
import sys
import os

def get_resource_path(relative_path):
    try:
        base_path = sys._MEIPASS
    except AttributeError:
        base_path = os.path.abspath(".")
    return os.path.join(base_path, relative_path)

# Usage:
logo = get_resource_path("logo.png")

sections.title: Unique Features (Birth Certificate, UV & Auto-Injector)
sections.content:
1. Birth Certificate Metadata Injection

Generates [Project]_birth_certificate.json containing the full package ledger and Python version directly into the build root, allowing applications to audit their compilation environment.

2. Standalone UV Runtime Bundling (uv.exe)

For applications that dynamically provision plugins at client sites, checking this embeds uv.exe via --add-binary for ultra-fast client-side package management.

3. VenvHub Auto-Injector (Local Packages)

When utilizing Local Packages (Linker), the builder preprocessor:

  • Parses venvhub.json and injects --paths flags for all linked codebases.
  • Injects --add-data arguments for every linked module, bundling all assets, JSON configs, and UI files automatically without manual configuration.

sections.title: Imports & Advanced Tuning (Hidden Imports, Excludes, UAC)
sections.content:
Hidden Imports

For dynamic imports loaded via importlib that bypass static analysis, add module names here to force bundle inclusion.

Exclude Modules

Strip unnecessary heavy dependencies (e.g. pandas, tkinter) pulled in as optional sub-dependencies to minimize binary footprint.

Advanced Flags:

  • Clean Cache (--clean): Purges stale build cache artifacts before compiling.
  • Request Elevation (--uac-admin): Embeds Windows Administrator UAC manifest into the executable header.

sections.title: Build Pipeline & Live Preview
sections.content:
Live CLI Preview

Inspects the generated PyInstaller command in real time with support for custom user arguments (e.g. --noupx).

Execution:

  1. Click 🛠 BUILD .EXE.
  2. Streams live compiler telemetry to the Build Log Dialog in an asynchronous worker thread.
  3. Upon completion (✅ DONE), final distributables are ready in the dist/ folder.
